subject: geography
title: Agriculture and food systems
objective: Connect climate, farming, and the food supply.

lesson.opening: Farming feeds the world, and what can be grown where depends on climate, soil, and technology.

sections.heading: Subsistence and commercial
sections.body: Subsistence farming feeds the farmer’s family; commercial farming sells for profit, often on a large scale.

sections.heading: Climate and crops
sections.body: Warm, wet climates suit rice and tropical crops; temperate climates suit wheat, maize, and livestock.

sections.heading: The Green Revolution
sections.body: New seeds, fertiliser, and irrigation raised yields sharply in the twentieth century, with uneven costs and benefits.

activities.prompt: Which is a commercial farming crop?
Explain how climate limits what can be farmed in a region.
activities.context: Temperature, rainfall, and growing season decide which crops a region can support.
